`unicorn-arm.mjs` is the ARM-only Unicorn.js 2.1.4 interpreter built from the pinned sources below. The bundled patch releases each temporary allocated when the Wasm helper adapter widens a 32-bit argument. The original adapter retained these until the end of a translation block. Long blocks instrumented for instruction counting could exhaust the translator's temporary pool.

The [Unicorn.js source and build script](https://github.com/AlexAltea/unicorn.js/tree/560284c59c11c8d6c94d537f4354339f069ddcdf) are by Alexandro Sanchez Bach and contributors. The [Unicorn CPU source](https://github.com/unicorn-engine/unicorn/tree/8028ec436f2d9376525352dd38ed9ed6b9f6be10) is by Nguyen Anh Quynh, Dang Hoang Vu and contributors, and incorporates portions of QEMU. The package ships under the GPLv2 license in `unicorn-LICENSE.txt`. Both source archives and the local C patch are in `source/`.

Run `scripts/rebuild-unicorn.sh` with Emscripten, CMake, Git, Python 3 and Make on PATH. This release was built with Debian Emscripten 3.1.69, LLVM 19.1.7 and Binaryen 120. The script packages the resulting single-file JS/Wasm with the browser/Node ES module adapter.

`texture2ddecoder.mjs` and `texture2ddecoder.wasm` are the unmodified WebAssembly wrapper (renamed .js → .mjs) and binary from [texture2ddecoder-wasm 1.2.6](https://registry.npmjs.org/texture2ddecoder-wasm/-/texture2ddecoder-wasm-1.2.6.tgz). The browser loads these only for PVRTC textures when the GPU lacks native compression support. See [pinned package source](https://github.com/fatal10110/unity-asset-reader/tree/15d1c8a33d057fc599f377b7af24e2cf3e8bc3c4/packages/decoder) and `texture2ddecoder-LICENSE.txt`.

`zlib-arm.mjs` contains upstream zlib 1.3.1 compiled as position-independent ARMv7 for the guest streaming ABI. Its allocator callbacks and working buffers live in guest memory. Rebuild with `python3 scripts/build-guest-zlib.py web/vendor/source/zlib-1.3.1.tar.gz` and LLVM 19 on PATH. The script checks the digest of the [Debian upstream source archive](https://deb.debian.org/debian/pool/main/z/zlib/zlib_1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1.orig.tar.gz). See `zlib-LICENSE.txt`.

`pako-zlib.mjs` bundles the low-level zlib routines from [Pako 1.0.11](https://github.com/nodeca/pako/tree/1.0.11). Run `python3 scripts/build-pako.py` to regenerate it from the bundled, digest-checked [npm source archive](https://registry.npmjs.org/pako/-/pako-1.0.11.tgz). The CommonJS source modules use inline module scopes for ESM. License notices are preserved in the source and in `pako-LICENSE.txt`.

CommonCrypto uses the digest implementations from [@noble/hashes 1.8.0](https://registry.npmjs.org/@noble/hashes/-/hashes-1.8.0.tgz) under the MIT license. The six ESM files used by the bridge are in `noble-hashes/`. The package's crypto import points to its sibling browser module.

`sqlite3.mjs`, `sqlite3.wasm` and `sqlite3-node.mjs` are the unmodified `dist/index.mjs`, `dist/sqlite3.wasm` and `dist/node.mjs` (renamed) from [@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm 3.54.1-build1](https://registry.npmjs.org/@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm/-/sqlite-wasm-3.54.1-build1.tgz) (integrity `sha512-foW427VBLJ3G87bsnvQTZCc9zYe0Fq1wH0pz1I6BlKLKXcArIAyTkHtq0iT2llmhcMQt9T/p6l5PpQQh+6O8uQ==`). The browser loads them only when a guest opens a SQLite database; tests use the Node build. `sqlite3.d.mts` declares only the API the libsqlite3 bridge uses. See `sqlite-LICENSE.txt`.
